name: Regulators

subjectOf.text: Congressional studies do not remedy regulators' informational disadvantage because they mostly follow after Congress has already identified concerns and may not provide real-time relevant information before regulatory action is necessary.
subjectOf.abstract: However, these studies mostly follow after Congress identified particular concerns in the regulatory structure or in financial markets. These studies may not provide real-time and relevant information before regulatory action by public rule-makers is necessary.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

subjectOf.text: Information exchange between agents of public rulemakers, such as regulators, will not necessarily involve decentralized information, unlike feedback effects between private and public rulemakers.
subjectOf.abstract: Unlike the feedback effects between private and public rulemakers, the information exchange between agents of public rulemakers, such as regulators, will not necessarily involve decentralized information.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

subjectOf.text: Greenwashing is curtailed in the impact certificate marketplace because any market participant can instantaneously invalidate nominal but not substantive impact stories published by certificate purchasers and by listed projects.
subjectOf.abstract: Through this transparency any form of nominal but not substantive impact stories published by impact certificate purchasers and impact certificate listing projects can be invalidated instantaneously by any market participant
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Impact Investing Innovation - From Impact 1.0 to 3.0 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4685567
scope_conditions: blockchain storage of impact certificate data

subjectOf.text: The personhood debate is mis-framed: the operative question is not whether an intelligent agent may hold a legal incident, but when holding it directly beats the best mediated alternative such as a guardian, trustee, insurer or regulator.
subjectOf.abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939
scope_conditions: allocation of a single legal incident
